attempts.summary: Configured node1 (SONiC) with routed addresses on both its non-management segments: eth1=192.168.1.1/24 facing node2, eth2=192.168.2.1/24 facing node3, with IPv4 forwarding enabled globally and per-interface. Made this persistent via ifupdown2 drop-ins (/etc/network/interfaces.d/eth1, eth2) and /etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb.conf, both applied automatically at boot with no manual reapplication step. node2 got a static IP 192.168.1.2/24 on enp8s0 plus a route to 192.168.2.0/24 via 192.168.1.1; node3 got 192.168.2.2/24 plus a route to 192.168.1.0/24 via 192.168.2.1 — both via nmcli, which is natively persistent on RHEL10. Verified node2<->node3 reachability through node1 before any restart, then restarted all three nodes one at a time (node1, then node2, then node3) using each OS's native reboot, confirmed each node's boot_id in /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id changed, and re-verified interface addresses, forwarding sysctls, routes, and end-to-end ping between node2 and node3 after each restart — including after node1 itself came back, proving the routed configuration returns on its own.
